easy.def: A box in a kitchen where food is baked.
examples: The cake is in the oven.

more.def: A closed space in a kitchen that is heated to bake or roast food.
examples: The bread baked in the oven for an hour.
Be careful, the oven is very hot.
Mom took the cookies out of the oven.
The bird flew over the house.
A bridge goes over the river.

more.def: Above something, or from one side of it to the other side.
examples: A rainbow arched over the hills after the storm.
The cat leaped over the fence and ran into the garden.
We hung a map over the desk.

more.def: Finished, or no longer going on.
examples: The rain is over, so we can play outside.
Our vacation was over too soon.
When the movie was over, everyone clapped.
It was a good year overall.

more.def: Looking at everything together; in general.
examples: Overall, I liked the trip, even though it rained one day.
The team did well overall this season.
Overall, the test was easy, but the last question was hard.
The overall cost was ten dollars.
The overall winner got a prize.

more.def: Including everything or everyone; taking the whole thing.
examples: The overall cost of the trip was fifty dollars.
The overall winner of the race received a gold medal.
I understand the overall idea, but not all of the small parts.

easy.def: Over the side of a boat.

more.def: Over the side of a ship or boat and into the water.
examples: A wave swept the crate overboard.
The sailor tossed the rope overboard.
A wave washed the bucket overboard.

more.def: A long, heavy, warm coat that is worn over other clothes in cold weather.
examples: He wore a long, heavy overcoat to keep warm in the snow.
I buttoned my overcoat against the cold wind.
The overcoat reached down to his knees.

more.def: To succeed in dealing with something that is hard.
examples: I overcame my fear of the dark.
She overcame her shyness and sang on stage.

easy.def: To do too much of something.

more.def: To do or use too much of something.
examples: Do not overdo the salt in the soup.
He overdid the exercise and was sore all day.
She overdid the decorations, and the room looked crowded.

easy.def: Late, past the day it was due.

more.def: Not returned or paid by the day it was meant to be.
examples: My library book is a week overdue, so I need to take it back today.
The overdue bill came in the mail on Monday.
The train was overdue by twenty minutes.

easy.def: To spill over the top because it is too full.

more.def: To flow over the edge of something because there is too much in it.
examples: The bathtub overflowed when I forgot to turn off the water.
The river overflowed its banks after the heavy rain.

more.def: In the sky or in a place above you.
examples: The plane roared overhead and then was gone.
Dark clouds gathered overhead as the storm came near.

more.def: Placed above your head.
examples: He put the bag in the overhead bin on the plane.
The overhead door of the garage rolled up.

more.def: To hear what other people are saying when they did not mean you to.
examples: I overheard them talking about a surprise.
She overheard the plan by mistake.
He overheard a secret in the hall.

easy.def: To put too much on something.
examples: Too many plugs overload the socket.

more.def: To put too much weight or too many things on something, more than it can safely carry or handle.
examples: Do not overload the backpack or the straps might break.
Plugging too many machines into one socket can overload it.
The teacher did not want to overload us with homework before the holiday.
It was an overload of toys.

more.def: A load that is too big, or too much of something for a person or machine to handle.
examples: The light went out because of an overload on the electric line.
After three tests in one day, I felt an overload of worries.
A paper overload jammed the printer.

more.def: To fail to notice something, or to look down on a view from above.
examples: I overlooked a mistake in my story.

more.def: For the whole night, or during the night.
examples: It snowed overnight and covered the street.

easy.def: Not as good as people say.

more.def: Thought of as better or more important than it really is.
examples: Some people said the movie was great, but I thought it was overrated.
The restaurant was crowded, but its food was overrated.
He said that the new toy was overrated and broke too easily.
He overreacted to the little bug.

more.def: To react in a way that is stronger than the situation needs.
examples: Do not overreact to a small spill.
He overreacted when he saw the tiny bug.
She overreacted to the small scratch.

easy.def: To change a decision made by someone else.

more.def: To decide against what someone else has said or decided.
examples: The judge overruled the earlier decision.
Mom overruled my plan to stay up late.
The coach overruled the player and called a time-out.

easy.def: To spread over and take over a place.

more.def: To spread over or fill a place in a way that is hard to control.
examples: Weeds overran the garden when we went away for the summer.
Ants overran the kitchen after we left out some crumbs.
The river overran its banks during the storm.

easy.def: To watch over a job to make sure it is done right.

more.def: To watch over people or work to make sure that everything is done properly.
examples: The teacher oversaw the class as they did their science project.
A manager oversees the workers at the factory.
Mom oversees the cooking when we make dinner.

easy.def: To sleep too long and wake up late.
examples: He overslept and missed the bus.

more.def: To sleep longer than you meant to, so that you wake up late.
examples: I overslept and missed the school bus.
She overslept because she forgot to set her alarm.
He was late because he overslept.

easy.def: To catch up and go past.

more.def: To catch up with someone or something moving ahead and then pass it.
examples: The faster runner overtook me near the finish line.
A bus overtook the truck on the hill.
Dark clouds overtook the sunny sky.

easy.def: To take power away from a ruler.

more.def: To take away the power of a ruler or a government, often by force.
examples: In the story, the people overthrew the cruel king.
The rebels tried to overthrow the government.
The old queen was overthrown by her brother.

more.def: Extra time that is added to a game, or extra hours at a job.
examples: Both teams played hard in overtime.

more.def: To turn over or upside down, or to change a decision.
examples: The little boat overturned in the strong waves.
The wind overturned the chairs on the porch.
The judge overturned the earlier decision.

easy.def: To be too much for someone.

more.def: To be so strong or large that you cannot cope, or to cover completely.
examples: The loud noise overwhelmed the baby.
Joy overwhelmed us when we won.

more.def: So strong or so great that it is hard to cope with.
examples: The overwhelming smell of paint filled the room.
The smell of smoke was overwhelming.
